mainTopic: Trapping from enclosures on יום טוב (מחוסר צידה), and animals of doubtful readiness (ספק מוכן) caught in traps
overview: This amud opens with the end of a משנה. Its rule is that an animal still needing to be caught (מחוסר צידה) may not be taken from an enclosure on יום טוב, while an animal already effectively caught may be taken. A ברייתא forbids trapping animals and birds from enclosures, which contradicts the משנה. For animals, the גמרא first says the two sources follow רבי יהודה and the חכמים, who argue about whether an enclosure counts as caught. For birds, the גמרא answers with a roofed versus unroofed enclosure, explaining that the 'house' rule applies only to the wild צפור דרור. It then solves the animal case the same way: a small enclosure is permitted and a large one is forbidden, and it gives three tests for 'small'. Next, שמואל rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, which prompts אביי's famous point that learning must be understood, not just recited. שמואל defines מחוסר צידה as needing a trap, and the גמרא refines this with geese, chickens and dovecote doves. Finally, a new משנה forbids taking from traps on יום טוב unless the animal was caught beforehand. The גמרא shows it is a מחלוקת about ספק מוכן, rules against רבן גמליאל, and begins citing other versions of that ruling, which continue on the next amud.

steps.title: The rule: if the animal still needs catching it is forbidden, otherwise permitted
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends with a general rule: an animal that is מחוסר צידה may not be taken on יום טוב, but one that is not מחוסר צידה may be taken.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the animal still requires catching, taking it is forbidden. If it does not still require catching, taking it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: We are at the end of the משנה, which gives a simple rule for deciding when you may take an animal from an enclosure on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is practical. If you would still have to chase the animal to grab it (for example, the enclosure is big or has hiding places), taking it counts as trapping and is forbidden. If you can just reach out and take it, it is already considered caught, so taking it is not trapping and is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Still lacking trapping; the animal still needs to be chased and caught
Enclosures or pens where animals or birds are kept

steps.whyThisMatters: This idea of whether an animal is already 'caught' is the key to the whole סוגיא. The coming argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים is really about whether an enclosure counts as 'caught.'

phrases.english: One that is lacking trapping — is forbidden,
phrases.notes: The animal would still need to be chased and caught.

phrases.english: and one that is not lacking trapping — is permitted.
phrases.notes: It can be grabbed immediately, so it already counts as caught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closing rule of the משנה, which earlier allowed trapping animals and birds from enclosures
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking an animal that still needs to be caught is forbidden on יום טוב. Taking one already effectively caught is permitted.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids trapping from animal and bird enclosures
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that forbids trapping from, or feeding, animals and birds in enclosures on יום טוב. This contradicts the משנה, which allowed it, for both animals and birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: And they pointed out a contradiction: From enclosures of animals and of birds, one may not trap on יום טוב, and one may not put food in front of them. This is a difficulty: animal against animal, and birds against birds!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite of the משנה and announces two separate contradictions: one about animals and one about birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allowed trapping animals and birds from ביברין and feeding them. The ברייתא forbids both. The גמרא treats animals and birds as two separate problems, because, as we will see, they may need different answers.

keyTerms.meaning: And they cast them against each other; introduces a contradiction between two sources
It is difficult; a contradiction or challenge
Animal against animal; the two sources contradict about wild animals

phrases.english: Gemara: And they raised a contradiction:
phrases.notes: Standard opening for setting one source against another.

phrases.english: Enclosures of animals and of birds —
one may not trap from them on a Festival
and one may not place food before them.
phrases.notes: Since they may not be taken today, they are not 'ready' for use, so one may not trouble oneself to feed them.

phrases.english: This is difficult: animal against animal,
this is difficult: birds against birds!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's permission by quoting a contradicting ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that one may trap animals and birds from enclosures and feed them on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules the exact opposite for the same case (enclosures of animals and birds), so the two sources clash, once for animals and once for birds.

steps.title: The animal contradiction is solved: two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: For animals, there is no real problem. The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה and the משנה follows the חכמים (רבנן).
steps.simpleTranslation: It is understandable that animal against animal is not difficult: this one is רבי יהודה, and that one is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the animal contradiction by saying the two sources simply follow two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא that forbids trapping follows רבי יהודה, who holds that an animal in an enclosure is not yet considered caught, so taking it is real trapping. The משנה that permits follows the רבנן, who hold that an enclosure already counts as caught. The proof for this split comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable; granted this part, but another part remains difficult
This one ... that one; assigning each source to a different opinion

steps.confusionAlert: The word בשלמא means only the animal case is solved here. The bird contradiction is raised in step 5 and resolved in steps 6-9.

phrases.english: Granted, animal against animal is not difficult:
this one is Rabbi Yehuda, that one is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא (forbids) follows רבי יהודה; the משנה (permits) follows the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the first half of the contradiction (animals) raised in step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the two sources to different תנאים (מחלוקת)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and ברייתא seemed to be one opinion contradicting itself about animals
steps.terutzMaskana: They are two opinions: the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה and the משנה follows the רבנן

steps.title: Proof: רבי יהודה and the חכמים disagree about whether an enclosure counts as caught
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה about trapping on שבת. רבי יהודה holds a person is liable for driving a deer into a house but not into an enclosure. The חכמים hold a person is liable for driving a deer even into an enclosure.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי יהודה says, one who traps a bird into a tower or a deer into a house is liable. Into a house he is liable, but into enclosures he is not. And the חכמים say: a bird into a tower, and a deer into a garden, a courtyard, or enclosures.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that רבי יהודה and the חכמים really do disagree about whether an animal in an enclosure counts as caught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, only a house fully catches a deer. An enclosure does not, so driving it there is not trapping, and taking it out of there later would be trapping, as in the ברייתא. For the חכמים, an enclosure already fully catches a deer, so taking it out on יום טוב is not trapping, as in the משנה. For a bird, both say only a tower (מגדל) counts, which hints at why the bird contradiction is harder (see step 5).

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה; introduces a source as proof
A tower or closet; a closed space where a bird is truly caught
The Sages, here arguing with רבי יהודה

steps.whatToRemember: For animals: רבי יהודה says an enclosure is not 'caught' (so the ברייתא forbids), and the חכמים say an enclosure is 'caught' (so the משנה permits). The bird contradiction is taken up in steps 5-9.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the יום טוב question of taking from an enclosure depends on the same idea as the שבת question of driving an animal in: whether the enclosure counts as having already caught the animal.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One who traps a bird into a tower
or a deer into a house — is liable.
Into a house is where he is liable,
phrases.notes: The גמרא's own inference from רבי יהודה's words.

phrases.english: but into enclosures — not.
phrases.notes: So for רבי יהודה, an enclosure does not count as caught.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
A bird — into a tower,
and a deer — into a garden, a courtyard, or enclosures.
phrases.notes: For the חכמים, an enclosure already counts as caught for a deer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 3 by showing that רבי יהודה and the רבנן disagree about enclosures
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה and the משנה follows the רבנן regarding animals in enclosures
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שבת: רבי יהודה makes one liable only for driving a deer into a house, while the חכמים make one liable even for driving it into an enclosure

steps.title: The bird contradiction is still unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The מחלוקת answer only works for animals. For birds, the משנה and ברייתא still clash.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the contradiction between birds in one source and birds in the other is still a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the bird half of the contradiction is still a problem. The answer from step 3 does not help here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the שבת משנה, רבי יהודה and רבנן argue only about a deer. For a bird they agree: a bird driven into a tower counts as trapped, but a bird driven into a house does not. So we cannot say the ברייתא follows one side and our משנה follows the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for 'against' (על). Here: one source set against the other

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think step 3 solved everything. It solved only the animal (חיה) side. The bird side is dealt with in steps 6-9.

phrases.english: But birds against birds is a difficulty!
phrases.notes: The ruling on birds in the משנה clashes with the ruling on birds in the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the תנאים answer from steps 3-4 cannot cover birds.
steps.kashyaTarget: The contradiction about birds between our משנה and the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both רבי יהודה and רבנן agree about birds, so the two sources cannot be split between them.

steps.title: Suggested answer: roofed versus unroofed enclosure
steps.stepSummary: A suggested answer: our משנה permits a bird in a roofed ביבר, and the ברייתא forbids a bird in an unroofed one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say this is also not a difficulty: this source is about a roofed enclosure, and that source is about an unroofed enclosure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an answer for birds: the two sources are talking about different kinds of enclosures. This answer is set up so the גמרא can test it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird in a roofed ביבר cannot fly away, so it is already 'caught', and taking it is allowed. A bird in an open ביבר can still fly out, so taking it counts as trapping, which is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a suggestion)
An enclosure or preserve for animals or birds

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָא נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: And if you will say: this too is not a difficulty:
This one is about a roofed enclosure,
phrases.notes: Our משנה permits it, because the bird is already caught.

phrases.english: That one is about an enclosure that is not roofed.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא forbids it, because the bird can still escape.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָא נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the bird קשיא of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): roofed versus unroofed enclosure
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources truly contradict each other about birds.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet accepted here. It is challenged right away in step 7.

steps.title: A house is like a roofed enclosure, yet a bird there is not trapped
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion fails. A house is like a roofed ביבר, and everyone agrees a bird in a house is not considered trapped.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a house is like a roofed enclosure, and according to both רבי יהודה and רבנן: a bird into a tower, yes; into a house, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the roofed-enclosure answer. It uses the שבת משנה about birds to do so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A house has a roof, just like a roofed ביבר. Yet the שבת משנה says a bird driven into a house is NOT considered trapped. So a roof alone does not make a bird 'caught', and the suggested answer seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: A tower. Here: a small closed space, like a closet or cage

phrases.english: But a house, which is like a roofed enclosure,
and according to both Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis:
a bird into a tower: yes,
phrases.notes: It counts as trapped.

phrases.english: into a house: no!
phrases.notes: It does not count as trapped, even though a house has a roof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer offered in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole roofed versus unroofed answer
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A roofed space (a house) still does not count as trapping a bird, according to the שבת משנה.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא: the house rule is about a free bird
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא explains that the שבת משנה is speaking about a צפור דרור, a bird that never submits. Only that bird is free inside a house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: Here we are dealing with a free bird, which does not accept authority.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא saves the roofed-enclosure answer. He says the 'house' rule in the שבת משנה is only about one special kind of bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צפור דרור keeps darting around even indoors, so it is not 'caught' in a house. Ordinary birds are caught in a house or a roofed ביבר. So the step 6 answer works again: roofed means permitted, unroofed means forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'free bird' (a sparrow or swallow) that is never tamed

steps.whyThisMatters: This limits the rule about a bird in a house to one wild species. That limit brings back the roofed versus unroofed distinction for regular birds.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
Here we are dealing with a free bird,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the שבת משנה, which says a bird in a house is not trapped.

phrases.english: which does not accept authority.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: הָכָא בְּצִפּוֹר דְּרוֹר עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the דחיה of step 7 and restores the answer of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: אוקימתא: limiting the opposing source to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A bird in a house is never trapped, so a roof does not matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a צפור דרור stays free in a house. Other birds are trapped under a roof, so roofed versus unroofed resolves the contradiction.

steps.title: Why it is called צפור דרור
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל explains the name: it 'dwells' in a house as freely as in a field.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Why is it called צפור דרור? Because it dwells in a house as in a field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבה בר רב הונא with a source. The source shows this bird stays free even indoors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name דרור is connected to the word דרה, 'dwells'. This bird lives inside a house just as freely as outside, so a house does not trap it. That proves the house rule fits this bird in particular.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל (a ברייתא)

phrases.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Why is it called a 'free bird' (dror)?
Because it dwells in a house as in a field.
phrases.notes: Wordplay: דרור and דרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim made in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That a צפור דרור is not caught even inside a house
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל explaining the bird's name

steps.title: Now the animal contradiction also has a size-based answer
steps.stepSummary: Following the same idea, the animal contradiction is solved without a מחלוקת: a small ביבר is permitted, and a large ביבר is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, animals against animals is also not a difficulty: this is about a small enclosure, and that is about a large enclosure.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the same approach, the גמרא gives a new answer for animals too. It no longer needs to say the sources disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (step 3), the animal contradiction was solved by splitting the sources between רבי יהודה and רבנן. Now both sources can agree. In a small ביבר the animal is easy to grab, so it is permitted. In a large ביבר it can still run away from you, so taking it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have arrived at this

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: birds depend on roofed versus unroofed, with a צפור דרור as an exception. Animals depend on a small versus a large ביבר. Neither our משנה nor the ברייתא needs to be a מחלוקת.
steps.confusionAlert: This replaces the step 3 approach as the answer for animals. It is a new way of answering, not something extra stacked on top of the מחלוקת.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
animal against animal is also not a difficulty:
This one is about a small enclosure,
phrases.notes: Our משנה permits it: the animal is easy to catch.

phrases.english: That one is about a large enclosure.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא forbids it: the animal can still avoid capture.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the case-splitting approach that worked for birds to give a new answer for animals.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both contradictions are solved by splitting the cases: roofed versus unroofed for birds, and small versus large ביבר for animals.

steps.title: What counts as a small enclosure and what counts as a large one?
steps.stepSummary: Having just said that a small ביבר is permitted and a large ביבר is forbidden, the גמרא asks how we measure 'small' and 'large'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a small enclosure? What is a large enclosure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a clear definition of the two kinds of ביבר from the last step. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 made the whole הלכה depend on the size of the ביבר. A rule like that is useless without a measurement, so the גמרא now asks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look in practice?
A small animal enclosure, where the animal already counts as trapped
A large animal enclosure, where the animal does not yet count as trapped

phrases.english: What are the circumstances of a small enclosure
and what are the circumstances of a large enclosure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definitions behind the small and large distinction made in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical test for telling a small ביבר from a large ביבר.

steps.title: First test: can you catch the animal in one lunge?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says that if a person can run after the animal and grab it in one bend or lunge, the ביבר is small. Anything else is large.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Any place where a person can run after the animal and reach it in one lunge is a small enclosure. Any other place is a large enclosure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the first answer: the test is how easily the animal can be caught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal can be grabbed in a single bend, it has nowhere real to escape, so it already counts as trapped. If catching it takes chasing and effort, the act is still real trapping, and real trapping is forbidden on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other, meaning any other case

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Any place where one runs after it
and reaches it in one stoop
is a small enclosure;
and any other is a large enclosure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A small ביבר is one where the animal can be reached in one lunge.

steps.title: Second test: are there corners for the animal to hide in?
steps.stepSummary: A second option: if the enclosure has many corners and nooks, it is large. If not, it is small.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps: any place that has many corners is a large enclosure, and any other place is a small enclosure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to measure, this time based on the enclosure's shape instead of its size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a fairly small space can let an animal escape if it has nooks to dodge into. So this test asks whether the animal has hiding places, not how many steps across the space is.

keyTerms.meaning: Or alternatively. Introduces another possible answer

phrases.english: Or perhaps:
any place where there are a series of corners
is a large enclosure;
and any other is a small enclosure.

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that the order flips here. In this test the case with the feature (corners) is the LARGE ביבר. In the first and third tests the case with the feature is the SMALL one.
steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא עוּקְצֵי עוּקְצֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second definition alongside רב אשי's first one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ביבר with many corners is large.

steps.title: Third test: do the walls' shadows overlap?
steps.stepSummary: A third option: if the shadows of the walls fall onto each other, the walls are close together and the ביבר is small. Otherwise it is large.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps: any place where the shadows of the walls fall on one another is a small enclosure, and any other place is a large enclosure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third possible test, which uses the walls' shadows to judge how narrow the space is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the walls stand close enough that their shadows overlap, the space is narrow and the animal is effectively trapped. This gives a visual measure in place of a chase.

phrases.english: Or perhaps:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּנָפְלִי טוּלָּא דְכֻתְלֵי אַהֲדָדֵי —
phrases.english: any place where the shadows of the walls fall upon each other
is a small enclosure;
and any other is a large enclosure.

steps.whatToRemember: There are three possible tests for a small ביבר: (1) the animal can be caught in one lunge, (2) there are no corners to hide in, (3) the walls' shadows overlap. In a small ביבר the animal already counts as trapped.
steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּנָפְלִי טוּלָּא דְכֻתְלֵי אַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third alternative definition.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ביבר whose walls' shadows overlap is small.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's opinion of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, that not all enclosures are the same. שמואל rules that the הלכה follows him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, not all enclosures are alike. רב יוסף said in the name of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and brings a ruling that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that whether an animal in a ביבר may be taken depends on whether it is already trapped. שמואל's ruling makes that view the practical הלכה. This sets up אביי's question about whether anyone actually argued.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows a certain opinion
Etc. The quote from the משנה continues

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Not all enclosures are alike, etc.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר לֹא כָּל הַבֵּיבָרִין שָׁוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic based on the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: an animal that is already trapped may be taken, and one that is not may not.

steps.title: אביי asks: does saying 'the הלכה follows' mean there was a dispute?
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that ruling 'the הלכה follows' someone normally implies that others disagree. So do the חכמים really argue with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: You say 'the הלכה follows him'. That implies they disagree!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי questions רב יוסף's ruling. He asks whether there is truly a disagreement, or whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is only explaining the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruling of 'הלכה כ...' makes sense only when there is a dispute to decide. If the חכמים agree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the ruling seems pointless. If they disagree, we need to know what they hold.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
'The halakha' implies that they disagree!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי הֲלָכָה מִכְּלָל דִּפְלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ruling in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the חכמים actually disagree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks what practical difference it makes
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers with his own question: either way the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so why does it matter whether there was a dispute?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: And what difference does it make to you?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes back on אביי's question. He claims it has no practical result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The practical outcome stays the same whether or not the חכמים disagree, because we act like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. So רב יוסף sees אביי's question as unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make to you?

phrases.english: He said to him:
And what difference does it make to you?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Dismisses the relevance of אביי's question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The need to ask אביי's question at all, not the ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The question seems to have no practical consequence.

steps.title: אביי: learning is not just singing a song
steps.stepSummary: אביי replies with a saying: should we just learn the words and repeat them like a song? Torah must be understood, even when nothing practical depends on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: 'Learn the lesson, and let it be like a song?!' Should I just repeat the ruling without understanding it?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his question. He says we have to understand the סוגיא, not only memorize the final ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing whether there is a dispute is part of truly understanding the משנה. אביי teaches that the goal of learning is understanding, not just knowing what to do.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn the learning, meaning memorize the text
Let it be a song, meaning recited without understanding

phrases.english: He said to him:
Learn the lesson, and let it be like a song?!

steps.whatToRemember: Even when there is no practical difference, we try to understand a סוגיא, including whether a ruling settles an actual dispute.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous statement of the value of learning for understanding, not just for practical rulings.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge to the value of אביי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Understanding matters in itself, so the question is worth asking.

steps.title: What does 'still needing trapping' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that anything מחוסר צידה is forbidden, and asks what that phrase means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: This is the rule: anything that still needs trapping, etc. What is a case of 'still needing trapping'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks for a definition. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a general rule built on the term מחוסר צידה. The גמרא wants a practical test for when an animal falls under that term.

keyTerms.meaning: Still lacking trapping, meaning not yet fully caught

phrases.english: This is the principle:
anything whose trapping is lacking, etc.
What are the circumstances of 'lacking trapping'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic based on the next phrase of the משנה.

steps.title: If you would say 'bring a trap', it is not yet trapped
steps.stepSummary: שמואל defines מחוסר צידה: any animal about which people would say 'bring a trap so we can catch it'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said in the name of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: Any animal about which one would say, 'Bring a trap and we will catch it.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question. If catching the animal needs a trap, it still counts as not yet caught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal you can simply pick up is already trapped. If you need a tool to catch it, you are still doing the act of trapping, which is forbidden on יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Anything about which one says, 'Bring a trap'
'and we will catch it.'

steps.whatToRemember: מחוסר צידה means the animal cannot be caught without a trap. Such an animal is forbidden to catch on יום טוב.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An animal that needs a trap to be caught is מחוסר צידה.

steps.title: אביי challenges the definition using geese and chickens
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that geese and chickens fit שמואל's definition of needing a trap, yet a ברייתא rules that trapping them is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But geese and chickens are animals about which people say 'bring a trap and let us catch it.' Yet a ברייתא teaches: one who traps geese, chickens, or domestic doves is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks שמואל's definition from Step 20 with a ברייתא. If 'needing a trap' made an animal untrapped, then catching geese and chickens should be real trapping, but the ברייתא says it is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Loose geese and chickens in a yard run away, so you might need a trap to grab them. By שמואל's test they should count as 'not yet trapped,' and catching them should be a real act of צידה. But the ברייתא says the person who catches them is פטור, which means they are already considered trapped. So 'needing a trap' cannot be the whole definition.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא (a teaching from the era of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself)
Domestic doves raised in the house (Herodian doves)
Exempt; not liable for violating שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Here פטור means these birds are treated as already trapped, so catching them is not the מלאכה of צידה. The point the גמרא needs is only that he is not liable for צידה. The ברייתא's wording does not by itself say whether catching them is fully permitted.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But aren't geese and chickens
creatures about which people say: bring a trap so we can catch it?
phrases.notes: This is exactly the wording of שמואל's definition from Step 20.

phrases.english: And it was taught in a ברייתא:
One who traps geese, chickens, or domestic doves
is exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְהָא אֲווֹזִין וְתַרְנְגוֹלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the definition of מחוסר צידה that שמואל gave in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's definition: anything about which people say 'bring a trap' counts as מחוסר צידה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Geese and chickens fit that test, yet a ברייתא treats them as already trapped (פטור). So the definition is too broad.

steps.title: First distinction: geese and chickens return to their coop at night
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא, quoting שמואל, says geese and chickens come back to their coop every evening, so they count as trapped. The animals in the משנה do not come back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said in the name of שמואל: These (geese and chickens) come into their coop in the evening, and these (the animals discussed in the משנה) do not come into their coop in the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by adding a condition. An animal that returns home on its own every night is treated as already trapped, even if it is hard to grab during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is that 'needing a trap' only matters for an animal that has no fixed home it returns to. Geese and chickens go back to their coop each night, so the owner effectively controls them already. The animals in the משנה's enclosures never return to a coop, so they are truly still 'untrapped.'

keyTerms.meaning: These (used twice to contrast two groups)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said that Shmuel said:
These (geese and chickens) come into their coop in the evening,
while these (the animals in the enclosures) do not come into their coop in the evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַלָּלוּ בָּאִין לִכְלוּבָן לָעֶרֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from Step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Geese and chickens seem to need a trap, so they should count as untrapped.
steps.terutzMaskana: Animals that return to their coop every night count as already trapped. שמואל's test only applies to animals with no such home.

steps.title: Challenge: dovecote doves also come home at night, yet one is liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: trapping dovecote doves and loft doves makes one חייב, even though they return to their coop every night. So returning home at night cannot be the key.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doves of a dovecote and doves of a loft come into their coop in the evening, and yet a ברייתא teaches: one who traps doves of a dovecote, doves of a loft, or birds nesting in pitchers in buildings is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the distinction from Step 22. Here are birds that do come home at night, yet the ברייתא treats them as untrapped, because catching them makes a person חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'returns home at night' made a bird already trapped, then dovecote doves should be like chickens and catching them should be פטור. But the ברייתא says חייב, so these birds are still considered free. That means the 'comes home at night' distinction is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Dovecote doves, kept in a coop but flying freely
Doves that nest in an attic or loft
Earthenware pitchers or jugs set up in walls for birds to nest in
Liable; has violated the מלאכה of צידה

phrases.english: But there are doves of a dovecote and doves of a loft,
which come into their coop in the evening,
and it was taught in a ברייתא:
One who traps doves of a dovecote or doves of a loft
or birds that nested in pitchers in buildings
is liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction just offered in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that coming home to a coop at night makes an animal count as already trapped.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dovecote doves come home at night, yet a ברייתא rules that catching them is חייב, so they count as untrapped. The proposed distinction fails.

steps.title: Refined distinction: the owner feeds geese and chickens
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא, quoting שמואל, refines the answer. Geese and chickens come home at night AND depend on their owner for food. Dovecote doves come home but find their own food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה בר רב הונא said in the name of שמואל: These (geese and chickens) come into their coop in the evening and their food is your responsibility. These (dovecote doves) come into their coop in the evening, but their food is not your responsibility.
steps.whatsHappening: The word אלא signals that the first answer is dropped and replaced with a better version. The deciding factor is now whether the owner feeds the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coming home at night alone is not enough. An animal counts as already trapped only if it also relies on its owner for food, because then it is used to him and fully under his control. Dovecote doves find their own food outside, so they are still independent, and catching them is real צידה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals that a previous answer is replaced
Their food is your responsibility (you feed them)

steps.whatToRemember: An animal is considered already trapped, so catching it is not צידה, when it both returns to its coop at night and is fed by its owner. Geese and chickens fit this. Dovecote doves come home but feed themselves, so catching them is real trapping.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical test for which domestic animals and birds may be caught on שבת and יום טוב without violating צידה.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rather, Rabba bar Rav Huna said that Shmuel said:
These (geese and chickens) come into their coop in the evening
and their food is your responsibility,
while these (dovecote doves) come into their coop in the evening
but their food is not your responsibility.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer from Step 22, which was knocked down in Step 23, with a refined distinction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Coming home at night alone makes an animal count as trapped.
steps.terutzMaskana: An animal counts as trapped only if it comes home at night and is also fed by its owner.

steps.title: רב מרי: Some birds run away and some do not
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי gives a different answer: dovecote doves tend to escape, while geese and chickens do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: These ones tend to run away, and those ones do not tend to run away.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי offers a second way to answer the question from Step 23. That question asked why dovecote doves are treated differently from geese and chickens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר רב הונא said the difference is about who feeds them. רב מרי says the difference is about behavior. Dovecote doves try to escape, so catching them is real trapping. Geese and chickens do not try to escape, so they already count as trapped.

keyTerms.meaning: they tend to / they usually do

phrases.english: Rav Mari said:
These tend to run away,
phrases.notes: the dovecote doves

phrases.english: and these do not tend to run away.
phrases.notes: geese and chickens

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative to רבה בר רב הונא's answer in Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New distinguishing factor (behavior instead of feeding)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Dovecote doves and chickens both come home at night, so they should be treated the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: Dovecote doves try to escape, so they still need trapping. Chickens and geese do not.

steps.title: But all birds run away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: chickens and geese also run when someone chases them.
steps.simpleTranslation: All of them also tend to run away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב מרי's distinction. Every bird runs when you chase it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If running away is the test, chickens should also need trapping, because they flee too. So 'running away' alone cannot be what separates the two groups.

phrases.english: All of them also tend to run away!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב מרי's distinction from Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מרי's claim that only dovecote doves run away
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every bird flees when chased, so running away cannot be the dividing line.

steps.title: They keep escaping even inside their coop
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי meant that dovecote doves keep running away even inside their coop. Chickens do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: We mean that they tend to run away even into their coop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens רב מרי's point. The issue is not running in the open field. It is how the bird acts once it is inside its coop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A chicken inside its coop stays put and is easy to grab, so it already counts as trapped. A dovecote dove keeps darting around even inside the coop, so catching it is still real trapping.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for why dovecote doves are different. רבה בר רב הונא says they find their own food. רב מרי says they keep escaping even inside their coop.

phrases.english: We are speaking about their coop,
that there they tend to run away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 26 by explaining what רב מרי meant.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב מרי meant that some birds run away in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant that they keep escaping even inside their own coop.

steps.title: משנה: Traps set before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: Traps set on ערב יום טוב may not be emptied on יום טוב unless you know the animals were caught before יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Traps for animals, birds, and fish that a person set on ערב יום טוב — he may not take from them on יום טוב, unless he knows they were caught on ערב יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that an animal found in a trap on יום טוב is forbidden unless you know it was caught before יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food used on יום טוב must be מוכן, meaning ready and available before יום טוב began. An animal still free when יום טוב started was not ready, even though the trap was set earlier. Only if you know it was caught before יום טוב may you take it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole topic of מוכן: food must be ready before יום טוב starts.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Traps for animals, birds, and fish
that he set on the eve of Yom Tov —
he may not take from them on Yom Tov,
unless he knows
that they were caught on the eve of Yom Tov.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְצוּדוֹת חַיָּה וְעוֹף וְדָגִים שֶׁעֲשָׂאָן מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה. It opens a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal in a trap is forbidden on יום טוב unless it is known to have been caught before יום טוב.

steps.title: משנה: רבן גמליאל and the gentile's fish
steps.stepSummary: A גוי brought fish to רבן גמליאל. He said the fish were permitted, but he did not want to accept them from that person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there was an incident with a certain gentile who brought fish to רבן גמליאל, and he said: They are permitted, but I do not wish to accept them from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a story about רבן גמליאל. He ruled that fish brought on יום טוב were permitted, though he personally refused them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It was not known whether these fish were caught before or during יום טוב. Even so, רבן גמליאל called them permitted. That seems to clash with the rule just stated, which is what the גמרא will ask about next.
steps.confusionAlert: רבן גמליאל did not refuse the fish because of any halachic problem. He said clearly that they were permitted. His refusal was personal: he did not want to take a gift from this particular person.

phrases.english: And there was an incident with a certain gentile
who brought fish to Rabban Gamliel,
and he said: They are permitted,
but I do not wish to accept them from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּגוֹי אֶחָד שֶׁהֵבִיא דָּגִים לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל ruled that fish of uncertain status brought on יום טוב were permitted.

steps.title: Does the story contradict the rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה can tell a story that goes against the rule it just taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: An incident to contradict?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by challenging the structure of the משנה. Normally a story is told to support a rule, not to argue against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule said doubtful catches are forbidden. The story has רבן גמליאל permitting fish whose catching time was unknown. A story that contradicts the rule it follows makes no sense as written.

phrases.english: Gemara:
An incident to contradict?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the two parts of the משנה fit together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A supporting story should match the rule. Here the story seems to permit what the rule forbids.

steps.title: The משנה is missing words
steps.stepSummary: The משנה should read: ספק מוכן is forbidden, but רבן גמליאל permits it, and the story shows his opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing something, and this is what it teaches: Something doubtfully prepared is forbidden, and רבן גמליאל permits it. And there was also an incident with a certain gentile who brought fish to רבן גמליאל, and he said: They are permitted, but I do not wish to accept them from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by filling in a missing line in the משנה. That line turns the story into support for רבן גמליאל's own opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added words create a מחלוקת. The first opinion forbids ספק מוכן, while רבן גמליאל permits it. Now the story does not contradict anything; it illustrates רבן גמליאל's side.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what it teaches
in doubt whether it was ready before יום טוב

steps.whatToRemember: With the missing words added, the משנה is a מחלוקת about ספק מוכן. The first opinion forbids it, and רבן גמליאל permits it.

phrases.english: It is missing something,
and this is what it teaches:
Something doubtfully prepared — is forbidden.
And Rabban Gamliel permits it.
And there was also an incident with a certain gentile
who brought fish to Rabban Gamliel,
and he said: They are permitted,
but I do not wish to accept them from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 30 by rewriting the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story contradicts the rule of the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The story supports רבן גמליאל's opinion in a מחלוקת about ספק מוכן.

steps.title: שמואל: The הלכה is not like רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quoting שמואל rules against רבן גמליאל, so ספק מוכן is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that שמואל said: The הלכה is not in accordance with רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives the practical ruling on the מחלוקת in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the הלכה is not like רבן גמליאל, the first opinion stands. Food that may have been caught on יום טוב is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is not in accordance with Rabban Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the מחלוקת that Step 31 revealed in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ספק מוכן is forbidden, against רבן גמליאל.

steps.title: Another version: שמואל's ruling was on a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Some say שמואל's ruling was said about a ברייתא in which רבן גמליאל permits ספק מוכן and רבי יהושע forbids it. There, שמואל said the halacha follows רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some teach it on this, as was taught in a ברייתא: Something doubtfully prepared — רבן גמליאל permits it and רבי יהושע forbids it. רב יהודה said that שמואל said: The הלכה is in accordance with רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a different tradition about where שמואל's ruling was originally said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, שמואל's ruling was attached to a ברייתא and phrased positively: like רבי יהושע. The practical result is the same, since ספק מוכן is forbidden. Only the source and the wording of the ruling change.

keyTerms.meaning: as was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: And some teach it
on this, as was taught in a baraita:
Something doubtfully prepared —
Rabban Gamliel permits it
and Rabbi Yehoshua forbids it.
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative tradition about where Step 32's ruling was said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The halacha follows רבי יהושע, so ספק מוכן is forbidden.

steps.title: A third version begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a third tradition about which ברייתא שמואל's ruling was said on. The ברייתא itself appears on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some teach it on this, as was taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to quote another ברייתא where some place שמואל's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same formula as Step 33, now introducing a third possible source. The ברייתא itself appears on the next amud.
